title: Khara's army

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shurpanakha, a joke, a wound, and the spiral beginning. Cruelty compounds. Today, the next link: her brother answers.

Shurpanakha reaches her brother Khara, who rules a garrison of rakshasas in the forest. She falls at his feet, bleeding, and tells him what happened. He sends fourteen warriors to kill the two brothers. Rama brings them all down. So she goes back to Khara, screaming at him for his weakness. This time Khara marches out himself, with his generals and an army. The text gives the number: fourteen thousand. The ground shakes. Dust covers the sun. Against them, in a clearing by a leaf hut: one man with a bow.
screen: `FOURTEEN WARRIORS FALL.` → `KHARA MARCHES OUT.` → `FOURTEEN THOUSAND.` → `ONE MAN WITH A BOW.`

segments.voice: Rama sees bad omens and makes his plan. He tells Lakshmana: take Sita to a cave in the hills, guard her, and don't come out. Lakshmana doesn't argue this time. Rama puts on his armor, strings his bow, and walks out alone. In Valmiki the sages and the heavenly beings gather in the sky to watch, afraid for him. The battle is enormous: arrows, chariots, a storm of weapons. And the text keeps coming back to one thing. Rama doesn't panic. He doesn't rush. He stands where he is and works. One by one the generals fall, then the army, then Khara himself. When it's over, Sita comes out of the cave and embraces him. This is an epic, and epics tell battles big; you don't have to picture it as a news report. The tradition reads Rama as Vishnu on earth, and it expects the impossible from him. Still, there's something here for people who will never hold a bow. The number didn't decide it. Fourteen thousand is a number designed to make you give up before you start. What decided it was a man who stayed steady, and took the next thing, and then the next. One more detail. One rakshasa escapes the battlefield and runs all the way to Lanka. The spiral isn't finished. Tomorrow, the news reaches the king.
screen: `TAKE SITA TO THE CAVE.` · `ONE MAN WALKS OUT ALONE.` · `HE STANDS WHERE HE IS AND WORKS.` · `ONE ESCAPES TO LANKA.` · then, large: `STEADY.`

segments.voice: Think of everything coming at you right now, the inbox, the bills, the worries, the to-do list, and let it feel like fourteen thousand. Don't fight it; sit steady, pick the smallest next thing, and hold only that. Everything else can wait for the next arrow.
Khara's army. Fourteen thousand against one; Rama stands steady and wins, and one survivor runs to Lanka.
Your line: steady. Fourteen thousand against him, and one man who didn't rush. That's forty-seven days.

howItsDone: Hindus who honor Rama as an avatar of Vishnu read his battles as signs of his divine power; many also draw from them the everyday lesson of staying calm under pressure.

what it means: a number designed to make you quit, and one man who stays steady and takes the next thing.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki's Aranya Kanda gives the fourteen thousand and names Khara's generals, Dushana and Trishiras; one rakshasa's escape carries the plot to Ravana.
